title: A guided protocol for phenotypic analyses in integrative taxonomy: application to Diplolaemus (Iguania: Leiosauridae) and the description of new species
content:
Abstract
Species delimitation is a central task in taxonomy, yet identifying independently evolving lineages remains methodologically challenging. Molecular data can accurately trace the history of lineages, while phenotypic traits are often valuable indicators of their evolutionary independence. Here, we present a structured protocol for phenotypic analyses within an integrative taxonomic framework, guided by statistical principles regarding how information is incorporated into analyses: that of unsupervised, semi-supervised, and supervised. We apply this approach to three distinct morphological datasets in the lizard genus Diplolaemus, which includes five described species and three additional candidate lineages. We identified species that stood out as the most morphologically distinct within the group, even in the absence or little prior information, whereas others exhibited high morphological variation and were indistinguishable based on certain traits. The progressive incorporation of information improved classification accuracy, ultimately enabling the distinction of most lineages. As a result, we describe two new species, Diplolaemus varicolor sp. nov. and Diplolaemus crypticus sp. nov., while finding no support for the evolutionary independence of the remaining lineage. Together, these findings demonstrate that a structured phenotypic approach can robustly support the evolutionary independence of most lineages and provides a transparent, replicable framework for phenotypic species delimitation in integrative taxonomy.
